use_case_name: Update the Facility Map and Displayed Devices

claims.content: To refresh the facility map on the screen every 2 seconds to display current device status information.

goal.raw_text: To refresh the facility map on the screen every 2 seconds to display current device status information.

claims.content: System Administrator
The RLCS shall support multiple users logged on, up to the limit of the number of users defined in the database.
The facility map on the screen shall refresh every 2 seconds but can be configurable within the database to more than 2 seconds by the user.
Not including device and network response times, requests from the GUI for status updates shall not exceed 2 seconds to update the GUI display.
The facility map on the screen is configured to refresh every 2 seconds, or at a user-configurable interval greater than 2 seconds.

trigger.raw_text: The facility map on the screen is configured to refresh every 2 seconds, or at a user-configurable interval greater than 2 seconds.

claims.content: The RLCS shall store, process, and retrieve all data necessary to operate the application software as well as generate current and historical reports of system operations.
The RLCS database stores information needed to operate the RLCS as well as historical transaction data to generate reports of system operations.
The RLCS application software shall update and read database tables to support system operations.
The RLCS application software shall update and read password and device rule data in encrypted format.
The Personnel Security Level entity stores information about the five attributes used to restrict access to the RLCS: Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.
Command levels are of three types: 'Status Only', 'Control', and 'Override'.
Users with 'Status Only' command level security may not issue any control commands at any level (device, macro, or super macro).
'Control' allows a user to issue control commands, and is a higher level of security.
'Override' allows a user to temporarily change the status of a device in the database for a configurable period of time in order to allow a command sequence to continue.
Commands shall be classified in these categories: (1) Device control commands, (2) Device Macro Commands, (3) Super Macro Commands, (4) Override Commands.
Device control commands are single commands that change the state of a device.
Device Macro Commands are a group of two or more sequentially executed commands that change the states of two or more closure devices.
Super Macro Commands are a group of two or more sequentially executed macros that change the states of an Entrance.
Override Commands are commands that force the status of a device to a temporary known state for the purpose of completing an operation which otherwise would not complete.

If a critical alarm is detected, the RLCS notification to the operator workstation shall occur within 2 seconds of alarm detection, and shall occur whether or not an operator is logged on to the system.

If device status information fails to be received from device sensors within 2 seconds of the status information being issued by the device sensor, the system must handle the delay as it exceeds the performance requirement.
If field devices fail to respond to commands from the RLCS within 12 seconds of the command confirmation being issued by the operator, the system encounters a response timeout exception.

If requests from the GUI for status updates exceed 2 seconds to update the GUI display (excluding device and network response times), the system fails to meet the display update performance requirement.
If the 'Track # of Failed Device Commands' function identifies a command failure, the system generates Command Failure Data and may initiate a retry sequence via 'Control Devices'.
The facility map on the screen has been refreshed to display the current device status information.
The GUI display update for status changes has been completed within 2 seconds (excluding device and network response times).
The field device status information logging to the database has been updated (occurring every 2 seconds or at a configurable interval).
